instruction.text: The bag allowance on Michele’s flight is 23 `kg` and her bag weighs 21 `kg`. Work out how many kilograms she has spare.
instruction.sound: The bag allowance on Michele’s flight is 23 kg and her bag weighs 21 kilograms. Work out how many kilograms she has spare.

instruction.text: Fey’s school backpack weighs 750 `g`. Martha’s backpack weighs 245 `g` less than Fey’s. Work out how much Martha’s backpack weighs.
instruction.sound: Fey’s school backpack weighs 750 grams. Martha’s backpack weighs 245 grams less than Fey’s. Work out how much Martha’s backpack weighs.

instruction.text: Jane needs 1.2 `kg` of peeled potatoes to make a roast dinner. A bag of potatoes weighs 300 `g`. Work out how many bags of potatoes she needs.
instruction.sound: Jane needs 1.2 kg of peeled potatoes to make a roast dinner. A bag of potatoes weighs 300 grams. Work out how many bags of potatoes she needs.

atoms.a: First, convert the kilograms into grams.
Next, divide the total amount Jane needs by the weight of one bag of potatoes.

instruction.text: Lionel weighs 54 `kg` and Atticus weighs 57 `kg`. Lionel says that they weigh 91 `kg` together. Round their weights to the nearest ten to check his calculation.
instruction.sound: Lionel weighs 54 kilograms and Atticus weighs 57 kilograms. Lionel says that they weigh 101 kilograms together. Round their weights to the nearest ten to check his calculation.

instruction.text: Is Lionel’s calculation likely to be correct?

Jim is making an apple pie. He has 227 `g` of apples leftover and uses 642 `g` of another bag of apples. He says that he now has 869 `g` of apples. Round the weights to the nearest ten to check his calculation.
instruction.sound: Jim is making an apple pie. He has 227 grams of apples leftover and uses 642 grams of another bag of apples. He says that he now has 869 grams of apples. Round the weights to the nearest ten to check his calculation.

instruction.text: Was Jim’s calculation likely to be correct?
